[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Product teams must translate a business requirement into a deployed, compliant, production-ready system by manually authoring application code, infrastructure code, CI/CD configuration, security configuration, and compliance metadata — a process that takes days to weeks for a standard workload type that Gainwell has approved and built many times before. This manual translation is a bottleneck that autonomous AI development is positioned to eliminate, but only when the solution space is constrained by a mature Golden Path catalog.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The Intent-to-Infrastructure Pipeline is the Phase 3 capability of the [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md). It is an automated pipeline that accepts a human-authored structured intent document, invokes an AI agent to select the appropriate Golden Path and parameterize it for the stated intent, generates a complete application and infrastructure stack, validates conformance across all four verification layers, and initiates deployment. Human authority is exercised at the intent document authorship stage only; the pipeline executes autonomously from there.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Organizations with a mature Golden Path catalog (Phase 2 of the Golden Path strategy or later) where all four verification layers are operational
- Standard workload types fully covered by a published, verified Golden Path
- Teams willing to accept AI-generated output as the starting implementation (with full conformance verification) rather than human-authored scaffolding
page_texts.7:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineers** responsible for designing and operating Golden Path pipelines and AI-assisted development infrastructure
- **DevOps Engineers** managing CI/CD automation, pipeline orchestration, and deployment workflows
- **Solutions Architects** evaluating intent-to-infrastructure automation for standard workload types
- **AI/ML Engineers** integrating large language model agents into software delivery pipelines
- **Data Engineers** designing structured intent schemas and validation pipelines for AI-generated artifacts
- **Site Reliability Engineers (SREs)** maintaining the verification layers and conformance gates that govern AI-generated output
page_texts.8:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Reduces time from structured requirement to deployed, tested, compliant system from days-to-weeks to hours for standard workload types
- Applies all four verification layers automatically — AI-generated output is governed with the same rigor as human-authored output
- Scales the engineering organization's throughput without proportional headcount increase
page_texts.10:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) defines a three-phase maturity trajectory. Phase 1 builds the Golden Path catalog; Phase 2 automates enforcement and integrates AI-assisted development; Phase 3 enables autonomous development and intent-to-infrastructure workflows. This pattern describes the Phase 3 pipeline — the capability that only becomes safe and achievable once Phases 1 and 2 are complete.

Intent-to-infrastructure is not a speculative future capability. The underlying AI models (Claude, GPT-4o, Gemini) are already capable of generating complete application and infrastructure stacks from structured requirements. The limiting factor at Gainwell is not model capability; it is the absence of the governance infrastructure (Golden Path catalog, verification layers, AI context integration) that makes AI-generated output trustworthy. This pattern defines how to operationalize intent-to-infrastructure once that infrastructure is in place.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The pipeline operates as a multi-stage GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines workflow. The input is a structured intent document (YAML/JSON) authored by a product team. The AI agent is invoked via API (Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, or equivalent) with the intent document, the Golden Path catalog specification, and the AI context files as its prompt context. The agent returns generated code artifacts in a structured format. Subsequent pipeline stages execute the four-layer verification chain before any deployment occurs.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without this pattern, the Golden Path catalog and verification infrastructure exist as static developer tooling — valuable, but requiring human developers to manually apply them. Teams still spend significant effort on infrastructure authoring, security configuration, and compliance wiring even when the Golden Path defines exactly what those should be. Intent-to-infrastructure automation converts this known, repeatable translation work into an automated pipeline execution, freeing human engineers for novel business logic and domain modeling.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- **Prerequisite dependency**: This pipeline only produces safe output when the Golden Path catalog, all four verification layers, and AI context integration (PTN-APP-GOV-002) are fully operational. Attempting to deploy this pipeline before those prerequisites are in place will produce unverified output.
- **Human authority at intent layer**: Human engineers must author the structured intent document. The pipeline does not accept free-text inputs — structured intent with explicit compliance scope and acceptance criteria is required to bound AI agent reasoning.
- **Verification is non-negotiable**: Every pipeline run executes all four verification layers regardless of the declared Golden Path. There is no bypass mode.
- **Rollback is automatic**: If any verification layer fails after generation, the pipeline does not proceed. Generated artifacts are preserved for review but no deployment occurs.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The Intent-to-Infrastructure Pipeline orchestrates five sequential stages: intent parsing and Golden Path selection, AI agent generation, four-layer verification, semantic validation, and deployment gate. Each stage's output gates the next. The pipeline is triggered by a pull request that introduces or updates a structured intent document. The human reviewer action is limited to reviewing and merging the intent document PR — all subsequent stages are automated.

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Intent-to-Infrastructure Pipeline                                            │
│                                                                               │
│  HUMAN                                                                        │
│  AUTHORITY  ──►  Intent Document PR  ──►  Intent Document (YAML)             │
│                            │                                                  │
│                            ▼                                                  │
│  STAGE 1: Intent Parser + Golden Path Selector                                │
│           - Parses structured intent                                          │
│           - Selects applicable Golden Path(s) from catalog                   │
│           - Resolves parameterization (name, sizing, integrations)            │
│           - Fails if no Golden Path covers the stated intent                  │
│                            │                                                  │
│                            ▼                                                  │
│  STAGE 2: AI Agent Generation                                                 │
│           - Invokes AI model with intent + catalog spec + context files       │
│           - Generates: app scaffold, Terraform, CI/CD, OpenAPI spec           │
│           - Tags all artifacts with provenance metadata (PTN-GOV-AI-005)      │
│                            │                                                  │
│                            ▼                                                  │
│  STAGE 3: Four-Layer Verification                                             │
│           L1: Architecture Conformance Gate (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001)               │
│           L2: Architecture Fitness Functions (PTN-APP-GOV-001)                │
│           L3: Policy-as-Code Enforcement (PTN-INFRA-GOV-002)                 │
│           All evidence ──────────────────────────────► Evidence Store         │
│           Any failure: pipeline halts, artifacts preserved for review         │
│                            │                                                  │
│  STAGE 4: Semantic Validation                                                 │
│           - AI reviews generated output against intent document               │
│           - Verifies stated acceptance criteria are structurally addressable  │
│           - Generates semantic validation report                               │
│                            │                                                  │
│  STAGE 5: Deployment Gate                                                     │
│           - All verification evidence attached to deployment PR               │
│           - Deployment PR requires approval to merge (human optional gate)    │
│           - On merge: deployment pipeline proceeds to target environment      │
│                                                                               │
│  LAYER 4: Runtime Invariant Monitors (PTN-APP-GOV-003)                       │
│           - Configured automatically for the deployed service                 │
│           - Activated after deployment                                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
page_texts.17:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Intent Parser | Parses the structured intent document and validates it against the intent schema; extracts compliance scope, integration requirements, acceptance criteria | Intent Schema |
| Golden Path Selector | Maps intent to one or more Golden Paths from the catalog based on workload class, compliance scope, and integration requirements; fails if no match | Golden Path Catalog (PTN-GOV-AI-001) |
| AI Generation Agent | Invokes the AI model via API with the intent, catalog spec, and context as prompt; receives structured output artifacts; writes to a generation workspace | AI model API, Context files (PTN-APP-GOV-002) |
| Verification Orchestrator | Executes the four-layer verification chain in sequence; halts on any failure; routes evidence to the evidence store | L1 (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001), L2 (PTN-APP-GOV-001), L3 (PTN-INFRA-GOV-002), L4 (PTN-APP-GOV-003) |
| Semantic Validator | Invokes a secondary AI review pass to verify the generated output conceptually satisfies the intent and acceptance criteria | AI model API |
| Deployment Gate | Assembles the deployment PR with all verification evidence; manages the optional human approval gate; triggers deployment on merge | CI/CD pipeline |
| Provenance Tagger | Tags all generated artifacts with model version, catalog version, intent document hash, and timestamp | AI Audit Provenance (PTN-GOV-AI-005) |
page_texts.18:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Product team authors a structured intent document and opens a pull request against the repository's `intents/` directory
2. On PR merge (human approves the intent): pipeline is triggered
3. Intent Parser validates the document and extracts parameterization
4. Golden Path Selector queries the catalog API and returns the best-match Golden Path specification
5. AI Generation Agent sends the full context package to the AI model API and receives generated artifacts
6. Provenance Tagger annotates all artifacts with metadata before verification
7. Verification Orchestrator runs L1 → L2 → L3 in sequence; any failure halts the pipeline
8. Semantic Validator runs the secondary review pass; adds the semantic validation report to the evidence package
9. Deployment Gate assembles a deployment PR with all evidence linked; the deploying engineer reviews and merges (or auto-merge is configured for low-risk environments)
10. On deployment: Verification Orchestrator activates L4 runtime monitors for the deployed service
page_texts.19:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Human deployment gate**: For production or high-compliance environments, the deployment PR requires explicit human merge approval even when all verification stages pass
- **Auto-merge for non-production**: For development and staging environments, the pipeline can be configured to auto-deploy when all verification stages pass, with zero human action required after intent document merge
- **Incremental generation**: For existing services adding a new capability, the pipeline generates the incremental change rather than the full service, and verification runs in diff mode

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

**Hard prerequisites — pipeline must not be deployed without these:**

- Golden Path Catalog Phase 2 complete (PTN-GOV-AI-001) — catalog published with machine-readable API, all target paths verified
- Architecture Conformance Gate operational (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001) — L1 verified working across pilot repositories
- Architecture Fitness Functions operational for target Golden Paths (PTN-APP-GOV-001) — L2 suites proven against reference implementations
- Policy-as-Code Enforcement operational (PTN-INFRA-GOV-002) — L3 policy library deployed with target path policies
- AI Agent Context Integration deployed for all target repositories (PTN-APP-GOV-002)
- AI Audit Provenance tagging operational (PTN-GOV-AI-005)
- AI Governance Policy published and adopted (PTN-GOV-AI-002)
- AI model API access secured and rate-limited (Azure OpenAI or Anthropic API with enterprise agreement)

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#phase-1-pipeline-foundation]

#### Phase 1: Pipeline Foundation

1. Define the structured intent document schema (YAML/JSON) — this is the human-AI interface definition; get this right before building the pipeline around it. The schema must require: workload class, compliance scope, integration requirements (upstream/downstream services), data classification, performance requirements, acceptance criteria, and team ownership.
2. Build the Intent Parser as a standalone validation tool (can be used by teams before opening a PR to validate their intent document)
3. Build the Golden Path Selector that queries the catalog API and returns the best-match path; implement a confidence scoring mechanism and a no-match handling procedure
4. Implement the AI Generation Agent integration: API client, prompt construction from intent + catalog spec + context files, structured output parsing
5. Implement Provenance Tagger: inject metadata into all generated artifact headers and a generation manifest file
page_texts.24:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#phase-2-verification-integration]

#### Phase 2: Verification Integration

1. Wire the Verification Orchestrator to the existing L1–L3 implementations; no new verification tools needed, just orchestration
2. Implement structured evidence collection: each verification layer's output is already evidence-store compatible; the orchestrator assembles the full evidence package for the pipeline run
3. Build the Semantic Validator: second AI invocation that reads the generated artifacts and the original intent document and produces a structured assessment of alignment. This is not a pass/fail gate — it produces a human-readable report linked to the deployment PR for the deployment approver to review.
4. Build the Deployment Gate: automated PR creation with evidence package, optional auto-merge configuration, L4 monitor activation on merge
page_texts.25:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#phase-3-organizational-adoption]

#### Phase 3: Organizational Adoption

1. Pilot with 2–3 volunteer product teams; measure: generation time, first-pass verification success rate, deployment success rate, semantic alignment satisfaction
2. Define the exception path for when no Golden Path matches the intent: currently routes to human architect for manual implementation or catalog extension request
3. Publish the pipeline as a reusable GitHub Actions workflow callable from any repository that has completed Golden Path onboarding
page_texts.26:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#deployment-gate-mode-decision-guide]

### Deployment Gate Mode Decision Guide

Use this guide to configure the appropriate deployment gate mode for each environment:

| Environment | Gate Mode | Trigger | Human Reviewer | Required Condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Development | Automatic merge | L1–L3 pass + seeded semantic validation | None required (optional notification) | L1–L3 all PASS; semantic rating is ALIGNED or NEEDS_REVIEW with auto-proceed flag |
| Development | Blocked | L1–L3 any FAIL | Engineering author | Must remediate before merge |
| Staging | Auto-merge with veto window | Dev 24h soak with no Layer 4 violations | Automatic unless vetoed within 24h | Dev soak CLEAN; L4 baseline established |
| Staging | Blocked | Dev soak has Layer 4 violations | Incident owner | Must resolve Layer 4 violations before staging promotion |
| Production (standard) | Mandatory approval | Staging 72h soak CLEAN | Change Advisory Board member | Staging soak CLEAN; complete evidence package attached to PR |
| Production (FedRAMP-High) | Mandatory approval | Staging 72h soak CLEAN | Designated FedRAMP Change Authority | Same as above + FedRAMP-specific evidence checklist signed off |
| Production (emergency) | Auto-deploy with immediate notification | Emergency incident declared | CISO notification; post-hoc CAB review | Emergency incident ticket number referenced; post-deploy audit required |

**Key principle:** Auto-deploy in non-production environments accelerates developer velocity. Mandatory human gates for production allow AI-generated deployments while maintaining human authorization accountability required by compliance frameworks.

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#example-1-structured-intent-document]

#### Example 1: Structured Intent Document

```yaml
# intents/eligibility-determination-service.yaml
intent:
  id: "INT-2026-0042"
  version: "1.0"
  authored_by: "benefits-platform@gainwell.com"
  date: "2026-03-09"

service:
  name: eligibility-determination-api
  description: >
    REST API that determines Medicaid eligibility for a member based on
    program rules, income thresholds, and household composition. Stores
    determinations in a managed PostgreSQL database with full audit trail.

workload:
  class: HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS
  language: java
  framework: spring-boot

compliance:
  scope:
    - HIPAA
    - Medicaid-Enterprise
  data_classification: PHI
  phi_fields:
    - member_id
    - date_of_birth
    - household_income
    - eligibility_status

integrations:
  upstream:
    - service: member-registry-api
      protocol: REST
      auth: IRSA-RBAC
  downstream:
    - service: audit-events
      protocol: Kafka
      topic: audit-events
    - service: eligibility-decisions-db
      type: PostgreSQL-Flexible-Server

performance:
  max_latency_p99_ms: 500
  target_availability_pct: 99.9

acceptance_criteria:
  - "GET /eligibility/{memberId} returns 200 with eligibility status and rule citation version"
  - "Every determination emits an audit event to the audit-events Kafka topic"
  - "No PHI appears in structured log output"
  - "Service starts and passes /health check within 30 seconds"
```

#### Example 2: Pipeline Trigger Configuration

```yaml
# .github/workflows/intent-to-infrastructure.yml
name: Intent-to-Infrastructure Pipeline
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['intents/**.yaml']

jobs:
  generate-and-verify:
    uses: gainwell/platform/.github/workflows/i2i-pipeline.yml@v1
    with:
      intent_file: ${{ github.event.head_commit.modified[0] }}
      catalog_url: ${{ vars.GOLDEN_PATH_CATALOG_URL }}
      deployment_environment: development
      human_approval_required: false  # auto-deploy to dev
    secrets:
      AI_MODEL_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY }}
      CATALOG_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CATALOG_API_TOKEN }}
      EVIDENCE_STORE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.EVIDENCE_STORE_TOKEN }}
```

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- The structured intent document schema is the most important design decision in this pattern. Invest significant effort in it before building the pipeline. It is the human-AI interface contract.
- Run the pipeline in generation-only mode (no deployment gate) for the first 4–6 weeks of adoption; review generated output manually before any deployment automation is enabled
- Track the "first-pass verification success rate" as the primary health metric for the pipeline. A rate < 80% indicates either the intent schema is allowing too much ambiguity or the AI context files need improvement
- Version the pipeline itself alongside the catalog. When a new catalog version introduces breaking path changes, a corresponding pipeline version bump is required.
- Retain all generated artifacts (including failed generation attempts) in the evidence store — the full trail of attempts is compliance evidence for the generation governance controls

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Deploying before prerequisites are operational**: The pipeline produces output; the verification layers determine whether that output is trustworthy. Without L1–L3 operational, the pipeline produces fast, unverified output.
- **Free-text intent inputs**: Natural language requirements without structured schema allow AI agents to make arbitrary technology choices. Structured intent documents constrain the choice space to what the schema allows.
- **No-match handling undefined**: When no Golden Path matches the intent, the pipeline must have a defined response — create a catalog extension request, route to human architect, or reject. An undefined no-match case produces unpredictable behavior.
- **Semantic validation treated as a pass/fail gate**: Semantic validation is a human-readable alignment check, not a structural gate. Treating it as a hard gate will create false failures for legitimate implementations that satisfy the intent via a different structural approach than the validator expects.
- **Skipping the pilot phase**: Rolling this pipeline to all teams without a pilot produces corrections at enterprise scale. Pilot with 2–3 teams, measure carefully, then scale.

page_texts.36:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

- All AI-generated artifacts must carry provenance metadata (PTN-GOV-AI-005) before verification begins — this is a non-negotiable pipeline requirement
- Intent documents must be retained alongside generation manifests and verification evidence for the full compliance evidence retention period (3 years minimum for HIPAA/FedRAMP scope)
- The AI model and API version used for each pipeline run must be recorded in the generation manifest — model changes must be reviewed by the Platform Engineering team and the AI Governance Committee before deployment
- For FedRAMP-High scoped workloads, the deployment gate always requires human approval; auto-merge is prohibited
page_texts.37:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

The pipeline itself (the I2I workflow template) requires ARB approval before enterprise rollout. Individual intent documents are approved by the team's engineering lead through the standard pull request process. The Golden Path Selector's "no-match" escalation path requires Platform Engineering team lead involvement.

A quarterly AI Governance Committee review of pipeline usage metrics, first-pass verification rates, and semantic validation outcomes is required.
page_texts.38:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|
| First-pass verification success rate | ≥ 85% within 3 months of pilot launch | Pipeline run records |
| Generation-to-deployment time (standard workloads) | < 4 hours | Pipeline stage timestamps |
| No-match rate (no Golden Path covers intent) | < 10% of pipeline runs | Golden Path Selector logs |
| Semantic validation alignment rate | ≥ 90% "ALIGNED" rating | Semantic validation reports |
| Production deployment defect rate (AI-generated vs human-authored) | ≤ human-authored baseline | Post-deployment incident tracking |

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** The Medicaid Enterprise team needs to build an eligibility determination service in Q2 2026. The use case is well-covered by the `HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1` Golden Path.

**Implementation:** A senior engineer authors a structured intent document (20-minute effort) and opens a PR. After review and merge, the pipeline runs. Stage 1 selects the Golden Path. Stage 2 generates the complete service stack in 8 minutes. Stage 3 runs all four verification layers — L1 passes, L2 passes, L3 passes. Stage 4 semantic validation rates the output as ALIGNED. The deployment PR lands with full evidence 35 minutes after the intent document merge.

**Outcome:** Complete, compliant, production-ready service deployed to development in under 1 hour. Human effort: 20 minutes intent authorship + 10 minutes deployment PR review. Previous equivalent effort: 3–5 developer-days.
page_texts.41:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** An AI agent generates a service that inadvertently violates the PHI log-scanning fitness function — the generated logging configuration writes full request bodies.

**Implementation:** Stage 3 fitness suite catches the PHI logging violation. The pipeline halts at L2. The generation artifacts are preserved with the violation detail. The pipeline registers the failure in the evidence store. The team reviews the violation report and either corrects the intent document context or re-runs with adjusted constraints.

**Outcome:** PHI logging violation caught before the service ever runs in any environment. Full evidence trail in the evidence store documents the attempt, the violation, and the remediation.
page_texts.42:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#real-world-example-3]

### Real-World Example 3

**Context:** The FedRAMP-High authorization boundary requires human review and explicit authorization for every deployment to production, even for AI-generated services that pass all 4 verification layers. The pipeline must support a mandatory human gate for prod deployments without blocking the developer experience for lower environments.

**Implementation:** The pipeline's deployment gate is configured with environment-specific modes: development is auto-merge (no human gate), staging is auto-merge with 24-hour notification window (humans can veto), production is mandatory human approval required. The production deployment PR includes the full evidence package (all 4 verification layer reports + semantic validation assessment) and is assigned to the designated FedRAMP Change Authority. The Change Authority reviews the semantic validation: "Design ALIGNED — the generated service implements the described eligibility API with correct PHI handling, audit event wiring, and FIPS-validated cryptography. Suggested review focus: confirm data-retention logic in ClaimsRetentionService is business-rule correct." The Change Authority approves in 25 minutes.

**Outcome:** FedRAMP-High authorization boundary human gate is satisfied without slowing developer velocity. Total time from intent document to production PR approval: 2.5 hours, compared to 5–7 developer-days for previous equivalent deployments. The Change Authority's review time focuses on the semantics — not the structure — because all structural verification is machine-proven.

#### Scenario 1: New Development Team Onboarding

A new team joining Gainwell with no prior platform knowledge can author their first service intent document using the schema template and have a deployable, compliant starting implementation in hours — without needing to understand Kubernetes, Terraform, External Secrets Operator, or Gainwell-specific security configurations. page_texts.45:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#scenario-2-catalog-extension-trigger]

#### Scenario 2: Catalog Extension Trigger

The pipeline surfaces a no-match: a team needs a `HIPAA-GRAPHQL-API-AKS` service type but no matching Golden Path exists. The no-match handler creates a catalog extension request in the Platform Engineering backlog. The team does not receive a generated service; they receive a clear indication that this workload type needs a new Golden Path to be authored. This is the correct behavior — no generation is better than unverified generation.
page_texts.46:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#scenario-3-multi-environment-deployment-path-orchestration]

#### Scenario 3: Multi-Environment Deployment Path Orchestration

A generated service for the provider-data team needs to progress through 3 environments: dev (auto-deploy), staging (auto-deploy with 24-hour soak window), prod (mandatory human approval). The pipeline is configured with an environment matrix strategy:

1. **Dev deploy**: Auto-merged immediately on L1–L4 pass + ALIGNED semantic rating. Dev environment receives the service within 45 minutes of intent document merge.
2. **Staging promotion**: Triggered automatically after 24-hour soak in dev with no Layer 4 invariant violations. The staging promotion PR is auto-merged if soak passes.
3. **Prod promotion**: Triggered after 72-hour soak in staging with no violations. Creates a production deployment PR assigned to the Change Advisory Board (CAB). The CAB sees the complete verification evidence chain including the 24-hour and 72-hour Layer 4 soak reports. CAB approves in 20 minutes.

Total time from intent document to production: 4.5 business days (dominated by the soak windows, not the generation or review time).

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

- **Standard workload implementation time**: 3–5 developer-days for a workload type covered by a pre-approved Golden Path; same architectural decisions are made repeatedly by different teams
- **Compliance wiring**: Developers unfamiliar with HIPAA-specific configurations (PHI redaction, ESO integration, audit event wiring) introduce errors that surface in fitness audits or production incidents
- **Human reviewer scope**: Architecture reviewers spend time verifying structural compliance properties (does the service have a health endpoint? are secrets injected correctly?) that are purely mechanical and could be automated
- **Evidence assembly**: Demonstrating compliance at deployment time requires manually assembling multiple documents; no single evidence package exists at deployment time
page_texts.49:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-001-intent-to-infrastructure-pipeline-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

- **Standard workload implementation time**: A workload covered by the catalog is generated, verified, and deployed to development in under 1 hour from a 20-minute intent document authoring effort; human velocity is redirected to intent specification and semantic review
- **Compliance wiring**: AI generation agent uses enterprise context loaded from the catalog and `.ai/context.yaml`; PHI redaction, ESO integration, and audit event wiring are correct by construction in the generated scaffold
- **Human reviewer scope**: Architecture reviewers receive a deployment PR with a complete machine-generated evidence package (all 4 verification layers passing) plus a semantic validation assessment; review focuses entirely on business logic and semantic alignment
- **Evidence assembly**: The deployment PR is the evidence package — all L1–L4 reports, semantic validation, and provenance records are generated automatically and linked in the PR description

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Standard, pre-approved workload types take 3–5 developer-days to deploy because the translation from requirement to compliant, production-ready system must be done manually even when the architecture is fully pre-approved.

**Solution:** An automated pipeline that accepts a structured human-authored intent document, invokes an AI agent to generate the full application and infrastructure stack from the applicable Golden Path, runs all four verification layers, and gates deployment — reducing standard workload delivery from days to hours.

**When to Use:**
- Organizations with mature Golden Path catalog and operational L1–L3 verification (Phase 2 complete)
- Standard workload types fully covered by a published, verified Golden Path
- Teams ready to adopt AI-generated output as the starting implementation

**Key Benefits:**
- Hours, not days, from intent to deployed, compliant system for standard workloads
- All four verification layers applied automatically — AI output is governed the same as human output
- Scales engineering throughput without proportional headcount increase

**Implementation Complexity:** High (prerequisite-dependent; cannot be safely deployed without L1–L3 operational)

**Prerequisites:** All 8 dependent patterns operational (see Dependencies section)

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-001, PTN-GOV-AI-002, PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-003, PTN-GOV-AI-005
